steps.title: Program.Main
steps.detail: First a handler for unhandled exceptions that writes CRASH.txt next to the exe — so a failure before the UI exists still leaves a trace. Then LibVLC is initialised, preferring the bundled libvlc/win-x64 over a system installation.

steps.title: OnFrameworkInitializationCompleted
steps.detail:
The real startup is queued with Dispatcher.UIThread.Post rather than run inline. The comment in the code gives the reason: it must not run before the message loop is alive.

OnExplicitShutdown matters because there is no main window yet — closing the login window must not end the process.

steps.title: AppConfig.Load()
steps.detail: Server address, port and the encrypted client key. If the file is missing, BuildDefault() writes one — including an encrypted literal client key that ships in the source.

steps.title: LoginWindow
steps.detail:
The window is shown and its Closed event completes the task, which is how an async flow waits on a window. See the Login flow.

Login happens before the launcher, so the user key is in AppData.CurrentUser by the time any per-user route is called.

steps.title: Load the settings
steps.detail: A null result is not treated as an error: the app builds a CreateSettingRequest with defaults — download path, dark mode off, scan on startup on — and creates the row through CreateSettingsAsync.

steps.title: Apply the theme
steps.detail: Set from DarkModeEnabled before the first real window appears, so there is no visible flash of the wrong theme.

steps.title: LauncherWindow
steps.detail: See the Launcher flow. The result decides between continuing and two different exit codes.

steps.title: LoadApplicationData
steps.sub: media and playlists, reconciled with disk
steps.detail: More than a load — see the Loading data flow. The exit handler desktop.Exit += OnExit is hooked here too.

steps.title: MainWindow opens
steps.detail: Now that a main window exists, closing it should end the app, so the shutdown mode is switched over. From here every action goes through MainWindowViewModel.

steps.title: Shutdown before the main window
steps.detail: 0 when the user chose to stop — cancelled login or cancelled launcher. 1 when the launcher hit a real error, e.g. no server answering.

steps.title: Username and password entered
steps.detail: The window offers both login and register; register calls login itself afterwards so the user never types the credentials twice.

steps.title: GetHealth()
steps.sub: is the server answering at all?
steps.detail: Checked before the credentials are sent, so „server not running“ produces a clear message instead of a failed login.

branches.label: no answer → error message, stay open

steps.title: POST /login
steps.detail: No key header on this route — it is one of the three the server leaves open, alongside /register and /health. Server-side the password is verified with bcrypt.

steps.title: Store the user, encrypt the key
steps.detail:
AppData.CurrentUser = new User(username, identifier, SecretProtector.Encrypt(user.ApiKey)). The key is encrypted the moment it arrives and only ever decrypted at the point a header is set, so plaintext is never held in a field.

From here every per-user call sends X-User-Key plus Auth with the identifier.

steps.title: LoginResult.Success
steps.detail: The Closed event completes the TaskCompletionSource the startup flow is awaiting.

steps.title: Login failed
steps.detail: The user can retry. Closing the window instead yields a result other than Success, and the startup flow shuts the app down with code 0.

steps.title: OnWindowReady
steps.detail:
Progress is reported through the Messages collection of LauncherMessage entries (title, text, icon) that the window renders as a list with status icons.

Note: the <summary> above this method also describes a Python install, venv, pip, requirements and Playwright browsers. Those are not implemented here — the five below are what runs.

steps.title: 1. IsServerRunning()
steps.detail: The one hard requirement. Everything the app does is an HTTP call, so without a server there is nothing to continue to.

steps.title: 2. EnsureVcRedist()
steps.detail: If missing, the installer is downloaded and run with /install /quiet /norestart. LibVLC needs it; without it playback fails in a way that is hard to diagnose.

steps.title: 3. RestoreDotnetPackages()
steps.detail: Finds the project files by walking up from the working directory. This assumes the app is running from inside the repository, which is the same assumption PyScrapperPath makes.

steps.title: 4. EnsureFfmpeg()
steps.detail: Needed twice later: IsSupportedCodec() calls ffprobe before playback, and MediaConverter calls both for conversion.

steps.title: 5. FinishSuccess()
steps.detail: Sets LauncherResult.Success, which lets the startup flow proceed to LoadApplicationData.

steps.title: ShowError
steps.sub: error panel with a close button
steps.detail: Reveals an error field in the window rather than throwing. The result becomes LauncherResult.Error and the app exits with code 1.

steps.title: Fetch the user's media
steps.detail: The server knows what the user had; the file system knows what is actually still there. The rest of this flow reconciles the two.

steps.title: Does the file still exist?
steps.detail: Entries whose path is literally "Does not exist" are on the removal list from the start — that is the marker the server uses for a record with no file behind it.

steps.title: .mp4? check the codec
steps.detail:
Only for .mp4, because that container can hold codecs LibVLC will not play.

Unsupported does not mean deleted: the entry stays with IsPlayable = false and a WARN in the log. It shows in the list but not in the playable set — and it is exactly what the converter exists for.

steps.title: AppData.AddDownloadedMedia()
steps.sub: the only intended way into the collections
steps.detail: Appends to DownloadedMedias and, when IsPlayable is set, to PlayableMedias as well. Views are bound to these collections directly, so the UI updates without any refresh logic.

steps.title: Load the playlists
steps.detail: For each playlist the assignments are resolved into the media objects already loaded above, which is why media has to come first.

steps.title: ScanFolderOnStartup?
steps.sub: a setting, off by default in a fresh config
steps.detail: When set, the download folder is scanned for files the database does not know about. MediaAlreadyExists(filePath) keeps a rescan from producing duplicates.

steps.title: Log two summaries
steps.sub: listed / playable / removed, and playlist count
steps.detail: Worth knowing when something looks missing in the UI: the counts in app.log tell you whether an entry was dropped for a missing file or merely marked unplayable.

steps.title: Removed from the local set
steps.sub: not deleted on the server — yet
steps.detail: The entry is dropped from the in-memory collections only. But because /save on exit is a full replacement, whatever was removed here is deleted server-side when the app closes normally.

steps.title: Which window opens?
steps.detail: ScrapWindowWithSearch for providers that support search — youtube, bandcamp, archive, soundcloud, newgrounds, youtubemusic. ScrapWindowWithoutSearch for the rest, where a URL is typed in.

steps.title: POST /search
steps.detail: Results carry url, title, thumbnail and type. The user selects one, which supplies the URL the download step needs.

steps.title: POST /download/video-audio
steps.detail:
The timeout on this client is set to 30 minutes, because the server resolves the media synchronously within the request — a browser-based provider really opens Chromium before answering.

The request always asks for stream. From the search window it also carries auto_convert; with it set the server delivers the file already in the selected container.

The response nests: DownloadResponse → DownloadResource → Context → OutputField / MediaInfoField.

branches.label: media type auto → 422 from the server

steps.title: Poll the progress URL
steps.sub: GET {resource.ProgressUrl} every 500 ms, in the background
steps.detail: The URL comes out of the response and is used verbatim — the client does not assemble it. StartProgress() starts a background task and returns at once, so the polling runs while the file is being fetched. It reports percentage, status and speed; a CancellationTokenSource ends the loop when the download completes or the window closes.

steps.title: Fetch the file
steps.detail:
HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead so a large file is not buffered fully into memory, plus a CancellationToken so the user can abort.

The file name is taken from the Content-Disposition header and appended to the path the caller passed — appended, not combined, which is why the path currently comes out without a separator. See Search and download on the workflows page.

steps.title: Extension as selected?
steps.sub: search window only, after the file is on disk
steps.detail:
The window compares the extension of the file that arrived with the selected media type and asks whether to keep a mismatch. The comparison includes the dot on one side and not on the other, so the question currently appears every time.

Then it waits for the file with at most ten File.Exists checks.

steps.title: POST /create/downloadedmedia
steps.detail: The record gets the path and the extension of the file that actually arrived. Note the ordering: the file exists locally before the record is created, so a failure here leaves an orphan file that the next folder scan will pick up.

steps.title: AddDownloadedMedia → list updates
steps.detail: The view is bound to the same ObservableCollection, so appending is all that is required for the entry to appear.

steps.title: 422 Unprocessable
steps.sub: the server refused the request body
steps.detail: Selecting auto sends empty strings for preferred_file and preferred_type. The server validates every non-null value and refuses empty strings, so the whole request fails before anything is resolved. SendScrapRequest shows the error detail in a message box.

steps.title: Choose a file and a target container
steps.detail: The picker filters come from AppData.ValidMediaTypes, split into media / audio / video / all. The target defaults to .mp4.

steps.title: ffprobe the streams and duration
steps.detail: The duration is needed for the percentage later; the codecs decide whether anything has to be re-encoded at all.

steps.title: Per stream: copy or re-encode?
steps.detail:
Three outcomes. The codec is already accepted by the target container → copy, no re-encode. It is not → the container's encoder from ContainerEncoders, e.g. .mp3 → libmp3lame -q:a 2. The target container is unknown → null, and the conversion is refused.

This is why an .mkv holding AAC converts to .mp4 almost instantly while the same file with Vorbis takes real time.

steps.title: Video needs re-encoding?
steps.detail: Video that cannot be copied goes through the fixed libx264 -crf 23 -preset fast -pix_fmt yuv420p. Converting into an audio-only container drops the video stream entirely.

steps.title: Run ffmpeg, parse stderr
steps.sub: progress lines vs the known duration
steps.detail: ffmpeg reports its position on stderr; against the duration from ffprobe that becomes a percentage. Cancelling sets the CancellationToken and terminates the process.

steps.title: Converted file returned
steps.detail: A file that failed IsSupportedCodec() at load time will usually be playable after this — that is the reason the converter exists.

steps.title: Refused or cancelled
steps.sub: logged, no exception to the UI
steps.detail: Consistent with the rest of the app: the model logs an ERROR line and returns a neutral value rather than throwing at the view model.

steps.title: desktop.Exit fires
steps.detail: Run synchronously, because the process must not terminate while the request is still in flight.

steps.title: Build one SaveDataRequest
steps.detail: The entire state in a single object. Nothing was written incrementally during the session, so this request is the persistence.

steps.title: POST /save
steps.detail:
Server-side this is a full replacement, not a merge: anything not in the request is deleted. See the Saving user data flow in the LocalServer documentation.

The consequence is worth stating plainly: if the app started with a failed data load and is then closed normally, it sends empty lists and the account is wiped.

steps.title: Exit code 0
steps.detail: The app also stops the server through /command where that is configured, which is why the server's quit_event exists.

steps.title: Exit code 1
steps.detail: An ERROR line goes to app.log. Since the session was never written incrementally, everything since the last clean exit is gone — the log is the only place that says so.
